statement: Choose the constants in the order specified at the end of this section. For every sufficiently large H, every admitted layer j ≥ 1, every admitted rectangle or bulk density of Definition 7.3, and either seam, the normalized block observation of Lemma 7.4 has an exact output in the same class, provided the output kinetic coefficients remain in the next admitted bands. In input normalization for the w coefficients, each of the four kinetic coefficients changes by α + κ/B + OL(H−1.05 j ), (7.11) where the direction and field indices are understood. The bounded coefficients α, κ and the next polynomial coefficients are given by the full-kernel Taylor map constructed below. 62 For a Brownian input and a flat reference input on common lists, their outputs satisfy, for fixed q∗ < 1 and c > 0, U′ ≤ q∗U + CLL−h + CLH−c j |λ|, |λ′ − λ| ≤ CLU + CLL−h + CLH−c j |λ|. (7.12) The coefficients in λ′ use output units, so the second estimate includes the real-coordinate conversion by T. No discrepancy of the old phase parameter is required. The restricted curvature cap renews with Fh+1 = Fh + cL p β pj. (7.13) Per output site, after the incoming scalar has been propagated, the scalar increment is 4(L2 − 1) log g + VL(lq, lw, χ, T, h) + OL(H−1 j ), (7.14) where VL is real, uniformly bounded and Lipschitz on the admitted bands. Its arguments may also specify the type of free history. There is no additional power of Pj.
